findings.summary: The Om navigation item never receives the current-page active state.
findings.consequence: On /dramawebben/om, the shared subpage navigation gives no visual current-page cue for Om, unlike Pjäser and Mer läsning; keyboard and low-vision users lose a consistent orientation affordance.
findings.evidence: DramawebbenShell accepts page "om", and app/pages/dramawebben/[document].vue passes :page="kind" for both om and kringtexter. In the owned template, Pjäser and Mer läsning bind active classes, but the Om <li> at line 35 has no :class binding. The stylesheet applies special current-page styling only through .subpage .links li.active a, and the existing behavior test currently expects zero active links for kind === "om".
findings.recommendation: Add the same current-page policy to the Om item, for example <li :class="{ active: page === 'om' }">, and update the behavior expectation so every local Dramawebben section exposes exactly one active navigation item.
